newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Worst seen over for Belgian OLOs.
newsitem.headline: Worst seen over for Belgian OLOs.

text.p: Belgian OLOs, rattled on Monday by the prospect of early French elections, will recover later this week as the French vote impact has now been largely discounted, analysts said.
Fears that the French government migh have an insufficient majority to carry through budget cuts required for EMU dragged markets lower and widened yield spreads against the Bund.

"The impact is largely discounted...The extra savings in France should have a supporting effect in the end," Kredietbank's Conrad Fieremans said. He also expected the OLO/Bund 10-year yield spread to narrow again.
Fieremans said sentiment was positive with prices expected to consolidate in the upcoming weeks as technically a rising wedge had been formed.
The European Commission was also likely to announce that Belgium was in a more comfortable position than France and Germany regarding its budget, he said.
An OLO/Bund spread of 14 basis points and OAT/Bunds spread of minus five was seen as a maximum level for now.
"There's no more substantial pressure from the early elections. The (OLO/Bund) spread should go back to 10 basis points, which seems a stable level," he said.

There was more good news from Germany where inflation figures and M3 money data revealed no nasty surprises. Any danger for OLOs was also unlikely to emerge in the United States with no major data there expected this week.
Fieremans said the swift rise of the spread had also been exacerbated by the lack of business, which was noticeable when the spread widened by two to three basis points at a time.
He was more negative for the longer term and expected the U.S. to outperform Europe in coming months.
The monthly auction, at which the 2007 OLOs and new January 2000 OLOs were up for sale, brought no excitement.
The Treasury sold nearly 25 billion francs in the competitive auction.
Traders said the auction had no real impact.
"It was pretty thin although price-setting was fairly good," said one, adding it pointed to a lack of interest in the market.
